newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain fears ETA could kill missing politician.
newsitem.headline: Spain fears ETA could kill missing politician.

text.p: Spain's Interior Ministry said on Thursday it feared a town councillor in the Basque region had been kidnapped by ETA Basque separatists who had threatened to kill him in 48 hours.

A caller saying he was from ETA told a director at Basque newspaper Egin, ETA's usual mouthpiece, that Popular Party politician Miguel Angel Blanco would be killed if the government did not move Basque prisoners nearer to their homeland.
A ministry spokesman confirmed that the call had been received and that Blanco had disappeared early in the day, but he could not confirm the kidnap.

"All the indications point to it, there was a call by the terrorist band ETA to Egin communicating the kidnap of Blanco and saying if the government doesn't move all the ETA prisoners closer to the Basque region before Saturday at 4 p.m. they will assassinate him," Cayetano Gonzalez said on state radio.

ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) has been pushing the Popular Party government to move imprisoned members to jails in the Basque region. Under a long-standing policy, they are scattered around the country.
Last week the separatists released a kidnapped businessman and hours later Spanish police rescued a prison worker who had held hostage by ETA for 532 days.
ETA, which has killed some 800 people in its nearly 30-year drive for Basque independence, had also abducted the prison worker to pressure the government on its ETA prison policy.
Egin alerted police on Thursday at about 6 p.m. (1600 GMT). The ministry said police were immediately deployed to search for the missing politician.
